summary: Your results across the board sit in the low-to-mid 40s, so this plan is about steady, targeted rebuilding rather than any single crisis. The good news is that the gaps are clearly linked: object-oriented foundations from CSE1OOF feed directly into the algorithms and data structures work in CSE2ALG, so improving one will lift the other. We'll start with the persistent Data Structures and Algorithms gap and the isolated Object-Oriented Design and Implementation gap, then work outward to your capstone (CSE3CAP) competencies. Every score here is a formative signal to guide what you revise next, not a verdict on you.

priorities.evidence: This is your lowest area and a persistent gap at 40.2% (CSE1OOF 42.6%, CSE2ALG 39.6%, stable across subjects). Your CSE2ALG:Central examination (38.0%) and CSE2ALG:Test (40.0%) were the weakest, with markers flagging implementing data structures and sorting/searching algorithms in Java and the overall objectives of the subject.
priorities.actions: Re-read the marker feedback on CSE2ALG:Central examination and CSE2ALG:Test, then re-attempt the exam-style questions tied to CSE2ALG:SILO2 and CSE2ALG:SILO3 by hand-tracing and then coding a search and a sort in Java. Rebuild the CSE2ALG:Assignment tasks as small well-tested examples, and for CSE2ALG:SILO4 write short comparisons of two data structures for a given problem to practise justifying choices.

priorities.evidence: An isolated gap at 42.6% in CSE1OOF, with your CSE1OOF:Practical demonstration lowest at 39.0% and CSE1OOF:Central examination at 43.0%. Markers repeatedly named code sharing and reuse (CSE1OOF:SILO3) and object-oriented design for real problems (CSE1OOF:SILO4) as areas needing revision.
priorities.actions: Revisit the CSE1OOF:Practical demonstration and CSE1OOF:Assignment feedback, then re-implement one real-life problem from scratch focusing on CSE1OOF:SILO4. Practise CSE1OOF:SILO3 by refactoring duplicated code into shared classes/inheritance in a small program, and redo the CSE1OOF:Test analysis/design questions for CSE1OOF:SILO1 to strengthen your object modelling.

priorities.evidence: An isolated gap at 45.0% in CSE3CAP, evidenced by your CSE3CAP:Assignment: Sprint Project management reports (45.0%), where the marker noted advanced project management during substantive development implementation (CSE3CAP:SILO1) needed revision.
priorities.actions: Re-read the feedback on CSE3CAP:Assignment: Sprint Project management reports and rewrite one sprint report to explicitly show planning, tracking and adjustment against milestones, addressing CSE3CAP:SILO1. Seek early feedback from your supervisor on this revised report before the next sprint.

priorities.evidence: An isolated gap at 46.2% in CSE3CAP. Your CSE3CAP:Oral presentation: Final Project Presentation (44.0%) scored below the CSE3CAP:Oral presentation: Project Milestone Presentation (48.0%), and the CSE3CAP:Assignment: Final written Project Report (47.0%) drew comments on professional documentation to industry standards.
priorities.actions: Compare feedback on your two oral presentations to see what dropped from the milestone to the final for CSE3CAP:SILO3, then rehearse a version tailored separately for technical and non-technical audiences. For CSE3CAP:SILO4, revise a section of the CSE3CAP:Assignment: Final written Project Report against an industry documentation template and seek early feedback on it.
